Google releases Gemini 4 Argon, called its most powerful model yet
Lucas Ropek
4:43 PM PDT · September 30, 2026
Google parent company Alphabet has
launched
Gemini 4 Argon, a new AI model built to handle a variety of tasks such as coding, research, and writing. But it’s cybersecurity that Gemini 4 Argon is supposed to have a particular knack for, according to Google.
Argon is only being rolled out to a select group of the company’s cyber partners through its Fairwind Program, Google’s security initiative. The model was trained specifically for defensive cyber work, and the company says it can “autonomously find, validate, and patch critical software vulnerabilities.”
Argon is also said to be good at coding and engineering, with the company noting that its own staff have already been using the model for their daily work, including debugging and codebase migrations. Google also touts Argon’s ability to parse visuals — whether that’s analyzing the contents of long videos or charts.
“Built to sustain deep reasoning across complex, long-horizon workflows, Argon is fundamentally changing the way we work and build at Google,” the company said
in a blog post
Wednesday.
Top AI labs have rushed to release increasingly powerful models, attempting to outdo each other even as those very same firms warn that AI could spin out of control. Not long ago, OpenAI
released Astra
— which it hailed as its best model yet. Earlier this year,
Anthropic’s Fable
was also released with similar rhetoric from the company.
Firms have done their best to market their services as superior to their competitors. In its blog, Google claims that Argon scored significantly higher than OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra and Anthropic’s Fable and Opus models across a variety of AI benchmarks. It cites Vals — an increasingly popular
AI benchmarking startup
— to show that Argon is currently the leading model on the company’s AI model index.
Once considered “
behind
” in the AI race, Google has recently enjoyed success with Gemini. The company announced in August that its app
had over a billion users per month
, a metric that makes it competitive with OpenAI, which also recently
announced
that ChatGPT had reached a billion monthly users.
